title: Robust constrained optimization of nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion in a biased-semiconductor cavity
authors: Mohamed R. Khodja, Belkacem E. Khodja
abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations offer a route to repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz forces. However, designs optimized only at nominal conditions may be fragile. We formulate repulsion in a planar PEC--vacuum--biased-GaAs--vacuum--PEC stack as a robust constrained optimization problem. The smaller of the outward pressures on the two conductors is maximized under fabrication and drive uncertainties. In the optically thick-slab limit, we prove that identical boundaries admit a symmetric optimizer, so equality of the optimal gaps emerges from the model rather than being imposed. At $300~\mathrm{K}$, with gap uncertainty of $\pm10~\mathrm{nm}$ and drive uncertainty of $\pm0.005$, the optimized design sustains a worst-case outward pressure of $2.257~\mathrm{mPa}$ and exceeds the corresponding far-field radiation-pressure plateau by $0.1812~\mathrm{mPa}$. At the nominal and active worst-case points, a full finite-slab scattering calculation agrees with the reduced model to within $1.60\times10^{-3}\%$. These results provide a design bound for cavity-enhanced nonequilibrium Casimir--Lifshitz repulsion and show how robust optimization can distinguish cavity enhancement from ordinary far-field radiation pressure.
summary: This work develops a robust optimization framework to maximize the repulsive Casimir-Lifshitz force generated in a biased semiconductor cavity. By treating the problem as a constrained optimization under fabrication and drive uncertainties, the authors determine optimal cavity parameters. The results establish a design bound for cavity-enhanced repulsion, demonstrating its superiority over simple far-field predictions.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of designing a semiconductor cavity to generate a robust, repulsive Casimir-Lifshitz force that remains strong despite uncertainties in fabrication gaps and external drive parameters.
main_result: The optimized design sustains a worst-case outward pressure of $2.257 	ext{ mPa}$ at $300 	ext{ K}$, which exceeds the corresponding far-field radiation-pressure plateau by a measurable amount.
method: The core method is formulating the problem as a robust constrained optimization, maximizing the minimum outward pressure across a defined uncertainty set.
model_or_system: The system is a planar structure consisting of two Perfect Electric Conductors (PECs) flanking a central, biased Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) semiconductor slab, creating a cavity.
key_observables: Outward outward pressure ($P_L, P_R$), which is decomposed into equilibrium and excess nonequilibrium contributions.
important_parameters: Gap uncertainties ($\pm 10 	ext{ nm}$), drive uncertainty ($\pm 0.005$), and the operating temperature ($300 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes the semiconductor response is passive and that the photon chemical potential ($\mu_\gamma$) is spatially uniform over the active regions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry (PEC-vacuum-semiconductor-vacuum-PEC) and show energy-resolved pressure components, while captions detail the selection of slab thickness based on reduction-validity indicators.
paper_structure: The paper builds the theory by decomposing the total pressure into equilibrium and nonequilibrium parts, develops the robust optimization framework, applies the optimization to find optimal gap sizes, and validates the reduced model against full finite-slab scattering calculations.
why_interesting: It provides a quantitative, robust design methodology for generating non-equilibrium forces, bridging quantum electrodynamics (Casimir effect) with semiconductor device physics and optimization theory.
